runtime: Chromium software WebGL2 via ANGLE SwiftShader
initialization: Stop renderer animation loop; ordinary game.start(); 30 updatePlaying(1/120) and updateVisuals(1/120,1) steps; no later simulation or visual update.

cameraPath.type: small lateral camera-only pan, smoothstep poses

captureMethod: game/scripts/qa-browser-capture.mjs canvasOnly actual WebGL2 pixel-pack buffer; bounded enqueue 60s, fence 60s, copy 60s. Stop after first failed capture.
limitations: Diagnostic camera-only inspection, not gameplay footage.
2 FPS is the authored capture cadence, not measured game or hardware FPS.
Software WebGL does not validate physical-device performance.
Six sampled camera poses are encoded directly; no interpolated or generated scene images.
Actual canvas capture excludes HTML overlays.
Gameplay and visual simulation are fixed after the initial 30 steps; this does not inspect actor animation, route completion, dynamic gameplay or cameraRig behavior.
Baseline dist does not contain build-info.json; source attribution must be read together with recorded frozen-tree provenance.
A 2 FPS sequence is a six-pose camera-path inspection and may appear stepped; it cannot establish temporal smoothness at a gameplay frame rate.
Natural pre-freeze visual clock differs by 0.2000 ms across the two runs; visual clocks remain fixed within each pan and were not overridden.
AFTER light stair/platform surfaces have low contrast, so these endpoints establish structural readability more clearly than fine material detail.

buildInfo.verificationScope: Exact source and package; source, campaign, production WebGL, UI and continuous video gate publication

case: camera QA readability: shorter pan avoids observed near wall

originalCase.occlusionLimitation: The final specified camera pose is dominated by a nearby wall/panel in both builds; visibility of the wider scene is limited.

proof.method: Every GitHub tracked blob independently hashed from game source bytes

before.distAttribution: Root confirmed this frozen game/dist was built from the verified baseline tree; exact served dist tree is independently SHA256 recorded.

after.sourceTreeAttribution: Root confirmed frozen art source bytes match the exact 14c commit tree; local HEAD attribution is not used as artifact identity.

captureSessionNotes: New independent shorter-pan level41 readability case; original level41 endpoint-occlusion case is preserved. One capture session; stop on first failure, no recapture. Per-frame metadata and report checkpoints are fsynced. Browser and HTTP server are created by the same Node process within one exec network/PID namespace.

RAWfirst/last scene readability passed for BEFORE and AFTER before video encoding. Original level41 X21→25 case was retained as the endpoint-occlusion evidence; this new case intentionally changes QA framing to X21→23.

preStartVisualClockDifference.note: Normal ready-state render loops before the requested freeze may leave slightly different visual clocks. No clock or game state override was used. Each build remains fixed throughout its camera pan.

endpointReadability.rawBeforeReview: Both endpoints show the staircase, overhead/cross beams, columns and depth of the multi-level scene. The right-edge wall/panel does not dominate the scene.
endpointReadability.rawAfterReview: Independent read-only reviewer inspected both RAWafter endpoints: staircase, beams, columns and multi-level depth remain readable. Right-edge panel does not obscure most of the image.
endpointReadability.encodedReview: First and last encoded output frames inspected: both panels retain a readable staircase, beams and depth, with aligned views and readable labels. No blank or dropped panel.
endpointReadability.detailLimitation: Light stair/platform surfaces in AFTER have low contrast; structure is easier to assess than fine material detail.

imageComparison.scope: Qualitative first/last readability inspection of real captured frames; no artistic acceptance or fine-detail quality metric.
visualObservations: Both specified endpoints retain meaningful views of staircase, support beams, columns and scene depth.
AFTER shows lighter stair/wall surfaces and cooler beam surfaces in the readable shared framing.
The shorter camera pan avoids the nearby wall/panel that dominated the original level41 endpoint at X25; the original case and its limitation are preserved.

video.title: before / after, camera inspection
video.composition: Each output frame horizontally stacks the same-index actual before and after JPEG; title panel added outside the scene. No temporal interpolation, invented scene frames or gameplay advancement.
video.visualQA: First and last encoded output frames inspected: both panels retain a readable staircase, beams and depth, with aligned views and readable labels. No blank or dropped panel.
video.encoding: ffmpeg libx264 crf18 yuv420p; six frames at 2FPS; no audio
